questions.stem:
The following code segment is intended to display the sum of the values in `nums`.

```text
FOR EACH n IN nums
{
   total ← 0
   total ← total + n
}
DISPLAY (total)
```

What is displayed when `nums` is `[3, 12, 11, 8]`, and why?

options.text: 8, because total is reset to 0 on every pass
options.why: Correct. The reset inside the loop discards the earlier values.

options.text: 3, because the loop stops after one pass
options.why: FOR EACH visits every element.

options.text: 0, because total is reset after the loop
options.why: The reset happens before the addition in each pass.
total is set back to 0 before each addition.

questions.explanation: Each pass sets total to 0 and then adds n, so only the last value, 8, remains. Moving `total ← 0` before the loop fixes it.

questions.stem: A network has computers P, Q, R, S, T, U. The direct connections are: P–Q, P–T, Q–R, Q–T, Q–U, R–U. What is the minimum number of connections that must fail for computer T to be unable to communicate with computer R?

options.why: After that many failures a path still remains.
Correct. Removing 2 well-chosen connections separates T from R; removing fewer always leaves a path.
Some set of 2 connections already disconnects them.
